Ethos and Values
The values of Guru Nanak Sikh Multi Academy Trust are encapsulated by the S.H.A.R.E acronym. These values are at the heart of everything we do as a school and they describe the qualities our pupils and staff value most.

About Us
Nanaksar Primary School opened in 2013 and forms part of the Guru Nanak Multi Academy Trust. It is a four form entry primary school, located next door to Guru Nanak Sikh Academy and in the London Borough of Hillingdon. The Multi Academy Trust has an exceptional track record of establishing successful schools. Nanaksar Primary aspires to be a strong part of this, providing the highest standard of education possible for all pupils.
In 2021 a brand new building for Nanaksar Primary School opened, including state of the art facilities and a spacious and nurturing learning environment for pupils. Facilities include a main hall, gym, dance studio, computing suite, cooking room and a 3G astroturf pitch.
At Nanaksar Primary School we strive to create the best learning opportunities for our pupils to help them grow academically, socially, spiritually and culturally. Upholding our commitment to work relentlessly to support our pupils in securing a very bright future for themselves, no matter how big or small the challenges that come their way, together, we triumph and overcome all barriers.
The school is hard-working, nurturing and friendly and takes pride in all its achievements. All pupils are encouraged to be the best versions of themselves and show courtesy and respect for others - themes that are central to the school ethos. Throughout the school, there is an emphasis on developing personal qualities, widening pupils’ horizons, and preparing for a purposeful and caring role in society. The school ensures that pupils are aware of the Sikh principles whilst celebrating diversity across all religions, with our SHARE values at the core of everything that we do.
We take great pride in expanding the Guru Nanak Sikh Multi Academy Trust, where Nanaksar Primary School warmly welcomes pupils of all faiths.

Pupil Premium and Sports Funding
The Pupil Premium Grant (PPG) is a sum of money which the school receives for every pupil who is currently in receipt of Free School Meals (FSM) or who has been in receipt of FSM over the past 6 years (Ever 6 FSM). Pupil Premium also covers those who are in the care of the Local Authority and those pupils that are children of service personnel. The main aim of the grant is to raise the achievement of children from disadvantaged backgrounds and to close the gap with their peers who are not entitled to this support. Nationally, children eligible for the grant achieve at a much lower level than their peers.
The Government believes that the PPG is the best way to address these underlying inequalities. In spending this funding, our key guiding principle is to ensure that all children entitled to Pupil Premium make outstanding progress, not just those who are lower attaining. Most of our pupils start school with little or no English and we aim for all children to make accelerated progress in order to reach or exceed age related expectations as they move up the school.
Our decision making is informed through analysing our data and regular parental engagement. We have planned the use of the Pupil Premium Grant to maximise progress and attainment, drawing on a range of resources.
Please see below for our latest Pupil Premium report.
NPS Pupil Premium Report 2025-2026
At Nanaksar Primary School we recognise the contribution of PE to the health and well-being of the children. We believe that a varied PE curriculum and extra-curricular opportunities have a positive influence on the concentration, attitude and academic achievement of all our children.
Our School Sport’s Funding will enable us to develop our provision in various ways. Please see below for our latest report.
NPS Sport Funding 2025-2026

Curriculum
At Nanaksar Primary School, we are committed to delivering a dynamic and innovative curriculum firmly rooted in our SHARE Values. Aligned with the national curriculum, our approach is centred on providing a broad and balanced educational experience that is both ambitious and challenging for all our pupils. Our curriculum is designed to nurture resilience, foster creativity, and enhance communication skills, equipping our pupils with the essential tools to thrive in an ever-evolving world.
Embracing the value of serving others (Seva), we instil a sense of social responsibility in our pupils, empowering them to become compassionate and engaged citizens. Central to our mission is promoting British values and fostering a solid foundation for ethical and democratic participation in a diverse society. With a relentless focus on excellence, we aspire to cultivate a learning environment that inspires curiosity and critical thinking, empowering our pupils to reach their full potential.
As we embark on our journey of continual improvement, we are dedicated to enhancing our curriculum to ensure it remains current, relevant, and responsive to the evolving needs of our learners.
Through a holistic and pupil-centred approach, we are dedicated to preparing our pupils for academic and personal success, instilling in them the values, skills, and knowledge they need to become confident, capable, and conscientious individuals. We are committed to fostering a culture of excellence, collaboration, and lifelong learning, propelling our school community towards a future filled with endless possibilities.
Our aspiration for every learner:
Through a broad, balanced and inclusive curriculum, we aim for all our pupils to ACQUIRE the knowledge and skills that enables them to ACHIEVE and flourish both academically and personally in every way. This will enable them to go on to ASPIRE and become confident, articulate and respectful citizens who contribute positively to society.

School Meals
We are fortunate to have high standards of school meals provision at Nanaksar Primary. Pupils can choose between having a hot or cold school meal, or can alternatively choose to bring their own packed lunch into school. All lunches cooked on the premises are vegetarian and planned according to Government guidelines. All food brought in from home must also be vegetarian and nut-free. Please see the school lunch menu below.
The Free School Meals provision has been extended to all Primary School Children until 2025 and we highly encourage them to have school lunches.
Please click on the link below to read the letter from the Mayor of London Mayor of London - UFSM 2024
We are a ‘Healthy Hillingdon’ school and as such, encourage healthy eating for all our pupils, staff and visitors. We do not allow sweets, chocolate bars, fizzy drinks and chewing gum at school. For NHS guidance on healthy lunchbox recipes - please click here.
The school participates in the National Schools Fruit and Vegetable Scheme and all Reception, Year 1 and Year 2 pupils are encouraged to eat free fruit or vegetables every day. Key Stage 2 Pupils can bring their own fruit or vegetable snack for break times.
Parents/Carers can subscribe to a Milk Scheme which enables their child to have a carton of milk delivered each day. To register for the Cool Milk scheme visit: www.coolmilk.com.

School Uniform
At NPS we have a strict uniform policy and a zero tolerance approach at the school which aims to give students a sense of pride and to aid the outstanding behaviour and reputation we already have. We are aware of the financial difficulties placed upon families. We are currently exploring ways of reducing unifom costs for all students across the Multi Academy Trust. If families are struggling to afford specific items of school uniform, we will endeavour to find second hand items in good condition through our Uniform Swap Shop. Please contact the admin office for futher support.
The uniform can be purchased from Fashion Mark, High Street, Southall, UB1 3HA (Telephone 020 8813 8841).

Attendance & Welfare
At Nanaksar Primary, we have high expectations for attendance and strive for pupils to achieve 100% throughout the year. Good attendance is proven to have a positive impact upon pupils’ learning. We do of course understand where pupils fall ill and need to stay at home.
We also request for your child to be dropped off promptly in the morning between 8.40am and 8.55am where we have a soft start. The school gate closes at 8.55am, so your child is in class and settled to start at 9.00am.
Letters are sent home to praise good attendance as well as to invite parents to a meeting where there are attendance concerns. We are keen to work in partnership with parents at all times.
We request that parents keep us regularly informed about any medical needs for their child, with their health and well-being being of paramount importance. Through close liaison with our welfare lead, we will work together to ensure that all measures are put in place to support the welfare and medical needs of your child. We aim for all pupils to be fully included within all aspects of school life, with no barriers to their participation.
